spec.notes: 5 x 5 tokens (1 x 1 window of 5) pooled to (1, 2, 3, 6): 50 stacked bins, read as a 10 x 5 grid of rows. Uneven bins: 5 -> 2, 5 -> 3, 5 -> 6 (PyTorch's start/end rule; they overlap). spec.notes: 1 contiguous group(s) of 8 input channel(s), K = 72 per group; the partials summed in double in group order 0..0, one float32 rounding. The 2 x 2-window raster makes every halo cross a window edge or the zero border. Exact: every product is a multiple of 2^-48 and every partial sum is below 18 < 2^5, so each group's dot and the group sum are exact in double in any order; one rounding. One group: the product is the unsplit convolution's im2col product.

spec.history: New fixture (P04): Milestone 10 found formulation B insensitive to the group order on its data (docs/history/upernet/notes/milestone10_findings.md, section 4, order study); this probe makes the order visible.
spec.notes: One output channel, weights designed: at token (7, 7) the 4 group partials are -0x1.0000000000000p+0, -0x1.8000000000000p-52, 0x1.0000000000000p+0, 0x1.8000000000000p-55 (one exact product each), and their double sum in group order, rounded once, differs from other orders and from rounding each partial. Exact: each group's partial is exact (one product), but the double group sum is inexact at the probe token and at about a third of the others; on this data the float32 result depends on the order only at the probe token. The mirror is exact because it adds the partials in the graph's order, in double, so the whole fixture rests on the premise that Earth Engine adds the double partial images in that order (Milestone 10, formulation B). If a probe fails while the 8 group fixtures pass, the premise failed, not the block.

spec.reference: torch.nn.functional.conv2d(padding=1) of the same unsplit (designed) weight
